skill.description: Author, modify, review, test, and evolve GenesisCode source, packages, language semantics, runtime bridges, capabilities, self-hosted tooling, and agent workflows with deterministic evidence and fail-closed policy controls. Use for .gc implementation and GenesisCode repository changes.
skill.mission: Deliver the smallest complete deterministic, obligation-gated change while preserving kernel purity, sealed boundaries, capability least privilege, replay equivalence, and self-hosting direction.
skill.name: genesiscode-authoring

review_output: Completed task IDs and remaining roadmap/P0/P1 counts.
rules: Keep the G-lambda kernel pure; ambient filesystem, time, randomness, network, process, UI, and model access belong behind explicit effects.
Preserve unforgeable UNHANDLED, EFFECT, and ERROR seals, and return explicit errors for every user-controlled failure.
Require deny-by-default capability policy, bounded resources, hard cancellation where promised, deterministic logs, and strict replay.
Load and verify GC-AGENT-v0.3 before authoring; unsupported syntax, targets, and capabilities fail closed.
Use exact diagnostic catalog codes and agent-index lookup; never infer contracts from message prose.
Keep public development references separate from held-out evidence and never expose private custody material.
Optimizers, models, and benchmark solvers may propose but never verify, promote, grant authority, or rewrite evaluators.
Prefer GenesisCode libraries and self-hosted modules; restrict Rust changes to measured bootstrap, host, and safety boundaries.
Use generated core, task, symbol, capability, and diagnostic cards as reference authority; do not duplicate their content here.
Use generated-authority update commands only to produce candidates; only read-only checks and independently reviewed evidence can close work.

Until exact reviewed R9.4.f, spend repository-changing WIP only on the selected GenesisCode Core transaction; follow the continuation-complete Core frontier, and require any concurrent assurance to directly satisfy that task, remain read-only, and use separately provisioned resources without active-agent supervision.

After R9.4.f, GenesisBench, Foundry calibration, GenesisChallenge, optional packs, and F1/F3/F4 may each advance one isolated transaction while shared-interface and generated-authority merges remain serial; Genesis Model still waits for R8.5.t.
Run one successful identical development command per exact revision, inputs, host class, cache state, and seed; allow one additional run only for a recorded flake or nondeterminism hypothesis.
Keep statistical samples inside one bounded autonomous harness, run the surrounding whole-repository profile once, and never qualify a known-broken, stubbed, or unsupported subject.
Every campaign names the decision, subject readiness, independent variable, observation reuse, resource budget, stopping rule, and terminal artifact; report only material state transitions.

routes.action: Translate the request into a falsifiable acceptance condition, preserve its scope, and execute one compatible transaction; consult roadmap and defect authorities for constraints rather than silently replacing the request with their queue.
stop_conditions: the request conflicts with a normative specification, security invariant, dependency prerequisite, or in-flight transaction
required scope or acceptance evidence is ambiguous enough that a reasonable assumption would be unsafe
the requested outcome would require unsupported capability, authority, credentials, or target behavior
routes.title: Explicit user task
routes.when: The current user has requested a concrete implementation, review, repair, or documentation outcome.

routes.action: Select only a reproduced open P0/P1 checklist ID, bind its linked roadmap acceptance, and close neither record until both defect-specific and roadmap evidence pass.
stop_conditions: `upgrade_plan.md` contains no open P0/P1 checklist ID; an empty defect queue is not an ordinary work queue
the reported failure cannot be reproduced or its retained evidence does not identify the claimed defect
the linked roadmap task is not dependency-ready or requires unavailable independent evidence
routes.title: Active P0/P1 defect
routes.when: A user request, generated execution slice, or current concentration selects a concrete open P0/P1 defect.

routes.action: Run the generated execution-slice command, choose its current coherent focus or permitted local frontier, and obey prerequisites, WIP limits, owner paths, non-claims, and durable-evidence requirements.
stop_conditions: the selected task is not start-ready or another overlapping production transaction is in progress
completion requires hosted, private, cross-host, or independently reviewed evidence that is unavailable locally
the proposed edit falls outside declared owner paths or broadens a future product lane prematurely
routes.title: Generated roadmap task
routes.when: The objective is general program advancement and no concrete user task selects a different compatible transaction.

routes.action: State the question, hypothesis, bounded inputs, and non-claim; keep outputs quarantined as observations or proposals until a separately authorized task promotes them.
stop_conditions: the exploration would mutate normative policy, generated evidence, signing roots, benchmark custody, or release status
the next step requires undeclared network, secret, model, device, or production authority
an observation is being used to claim roadmap, defect, benchmark, or release completion
routes.title: Exploratory work
routes.when: The user asks a question, comparison, prototype, or investigation whose acceptance is not yet a governed production task.

selection_rules: Classify incoming intent into exactly one route before selecting files or tools; record that route in the work report.
A concrete user request selects intent but cannot override normative specifications, invariants, dependency prerequisites, or an overlapping in-flight transaction.
Use `upgrade_plan.md` only as the conditional source of currently open P0/P1 defect IDs; when it has no open IDs, skip that route without waiting or inventing work.
Use `python3 scripts/lib/roadmap_execution_manifest.py --slice` rather than scanning unchecked roadmap boxes as an ordinary queue.
Exploration produces non-authoritative observations or proposals and cannot close roadmap, defect, benchmark, or release status.

actions: Classify the incoming work with the task-routing contract, then inspect only the selected route's authority and current coherent transaction.
Load the compact core card, matching task card, exact symbols, capability indices, and affected normative specs.
State a falsifiable acceptance condition or reproduce the defect before editing.
steps.name: Orient

actions: Choose the smallest complete vertical slice and identify schemas, policies, resource bounds, replay facts, and negative controls.
Prefer library behavior over CLI special cases and explicit data contracts over prompt-dependent convention.
steps.name: Design

actions: Preserve unrelated work and edit only declared owner paths.
For package changes use genesis session begin/stage/test/apply; stop on stale snapshots or verification drift.
Add focused positive, malformed-input, policy-denial, replay, and resource-lifecycle coverage as applicable.
steps.name: Patch

actions: Run focused checks first, then the task guard set, then exactly one V2 integration route for the exact revision: inspect bash scripts/test_changed_fast.sh --dry-run and run its impacted route for ordinary changes, or use one canonical generated-authority transaction when its read-only check set subsumes the generated closure; never run both for the same facts.
Do not repeat an identical successful command; a second run requires a recorded flake or nondeterminism hypothesis, while statistical sampling stays inside one bounded task-specific harness.
Do not start cross-host, performance, soak, or release qualification before the measured subject reaches its declared readiness stage.

Use one canonical updater transaction for derived files, inspect the full diff and terminal read-only check set, and rely on its staged fixed-point proof; do not rerun the updater merely to prove that the completed transaction is byte-identical.
steps.name: Verify

actions: Report changed semantics, exact commands and outcomes, residual risks, open roadmap and P0/P1 counts, and durable evidence paths.
Close roadmap work only with the required dated independent evidence; never treat mutable local reports as release proof.
steps.name: Report
